translations.about_md:
# Description

Mk48.io is an online multiplayer ship combat game created by Softbear. It is free to play in a web browser, with no install required. The goal is to level up your ship by collecting crates and sinking other ships. There are [# boats](/ships/) and [#](weapons) weapon types to choose from, spread over [# progressively more powerful levels](/levels/).

To learn more about the game, visit the [help page](/help/).
translations.help_md:
# Summary

#ifndef OFFLINE_ONLY
Mk48.io is a multiplayer naval combat game.  You start off a small ship and
consume crates to increase your score, which levels up your ship.  You have to go
find the crates: they float in the water, and you collect one by sailing into it.
While a small amount of crates spawn naturally, sinking other ships directly
increases your score and spawns many more collectibles.  Watch out for torpedoes!

#endif
To play, pick a game mode on the splash screen.  If applicable and desired,
adjust the region, server, or starting ship.  Then press **Play**.

#ifndef OFFLINE_ONLY
## Play with friends

There are 3 ways to play with friends:

* Accept an invitation from your friends and play on the server it connects you to.
* Invite friends to play with you on a public server.
* Create a party server and invite friends to play on it.

#endif
# Movement

There are four ways to move your ship:

* Right click, and optionally hold — **this is the recommended way to move**.
* Left click and hold.
* Tap and hold, on a touch screen.
* **WASD** or the arrow keys, with **X** to stop.

Once your ship is moving in a direction it will keep moving, so you can focus on
using your weapons.

With mouse controls, your ship turns to point toward your cursor, and you control
its speed by varying the distance between the cursor and your ship — near the
ship is slow, far away is full speed.  A quick left click fires rather than
steering, so only a *held* button changes course.  Level 1 ships cannot reverse
with mouse controls.

## Default Key Bindings

All keys can be rebound in the Controls settings.

* **WASD** or arrows to steer (**W**/**Up** forward, **S**/**Down** reverse, **A**/**D** turn)
* **RMB** (right click) held, or **LMB** held past the click threshold, to steer toward the cursor
* **LMB** (left click), **Space**, or **E** to fire the selected armament
* **X** to stop
* **1**-**6** to select an armament group
* **Tab** to cycle to the next armament
* **R** to surface (submarines)
* **Z** to toggle active sensors
* **C** to pay

Pinch to zoom out for a better view on a touch screen; with a mouse, scroll.

# Ships

Just like in real life there are many different types of ships, each with
different advantages:

* **Motor-torpedo boats** occupy the lower levels and generally carry multiple
  torpedoes and possibly guns.
* **Corvettes** and **destroyers** are larger and carry more weapons, including
  slightly more powerful guns.
* **Cruisers** are a compromise between destroyers and battleships.
* **Battleships** and **dreadnoughts** are very formidable ships, having
  extremely powerful main cannons.  They may carry a minimal complement of
  aircraft for submarine defense.
* **Submarines** travel underwater, making them immune to certain types of
  weapons, but must surface to fire certain types of weapons.
* **Hovercraft** can travel on both land and water.
* **Rams** are specially designed to ram other ships.
* **Dredgers** can modify the land.  New land is created by clicking in front of
  them, and old land is destroyed by sailing over it.
* **Icebreakers** plow through ice and snow without taking damage.
* **Minelayers** dispense magnetic mines that can help guard a small area.
* **Aircraft carriers** command a squadron of aircraft which follow your mouse
  cursor to attack enemy ships.

See the [ship reference](/ships/) for the full roster and its statistics —
length, draft, speed, health, stealth, torpedo resistance, maximum depth, and
the range, damage, lifespan, and reload of each weapon.

Note that certain values are approximate and may be affected by other factors.
For example, weapon damage depends on hit location.

## Upgrading

Once you earn enough points you can pick an upgrade from the top-middle of the
screen.  Be careful when upgrading: becoming a larger ship may lead to crashing
into land, or to reduced mobility if the water is too shallow.

Enemies are more likely to detect larger ships.  However, a few ships have a
property known as stealth to help you evade detection.

Not every ship is available everywhere — a few are restricted to certain areas,
and some are NPC only.

# Weapons

There are multiple different types of weapons available on various ships.  In
general, weapons are fired by clicking in the appropriate direction, although
**Space** or **E** can also be used.  Select an armament group with **1**-**6**,
or cycle with **Tab**.

* **Torpedoes** are powerful underwater weapons.  Some can track targets
  automatically, with sonar.
* **Missiles** are airborne and are faster, but less maneuverable than torpedoes.
* **Ballistic missiles** boost to much higher than missiles, can cross mountains in their midcourse phase, and attack targets from above in their terminal phase.
* **Rockets** are like missiles but lack guidance.
* **Rocket torpedoes** deploy a torpedo when in the vicinity of an enemy submarine.
* **SAMs** (surface-to-air missiles) can shoot down aircraft and missiles.
* **Gun turrets** shoot very fast shells that do moderate damage.
* **Depth charges** are stationary weapons that can be deployed against pursuing
  ships or submerged submarines.
* **Mines** are like depth charges but last much longer and are more damaging.
* **Aircraft** fly towards your mouse cursor and automatically deploy weapons of
  their own.
* **Anti-aircraft** guns defend against aircraft that get too close.
* **Depositors** create new land.  We'll let you figure out if this can be used
  as a weapon.

Once fired, all weapons take some time to reload.  Each type of weapon and each
turret reloads independently.  Consuming crates speeds up reloading.

# Sensors

All ships have some combination of sensors to identify other ships and obstacles:

* **Visual** tracks all targets, with a range that depends on conditions.
* **Radar** tracks targets above water.
* **Sonar** tracks underwater targets.

There are two modes for sensors, active and passive.  Passive mode listens for
emissions (e.g. sound in the case of sonar) from other entities.  Active mode
emits a signal and resolves contacts based on the signals that bounce back.  In
general, active mode allows you to see more, but has the potential to give away
your position.  Toggle between the modes with **Z**.

A contact your sensors cannot identify — one at the edge of your range, say — is
drawn as a plain marker pointed along its heading.  You know something is there,
and which way it is going, but not what it is.

# Fleets

You can join other players to form a fleet, using the panel in the top left
corner of the screen.  As the creator of a fleet, you can accept or deny those
who request to join it.  **Members of a fleet cannot hurt each other with
weapons.**

Fleets have a limited capacity that grows with the number of players online,
from 4 members up to 8 on a busy server.  In `2 Fleets` the two standing fleets
have no such limit.

# Game Modes

* **Fleet FFA** — free for all naval combat with small fleets.  A fleet is
  whoever you made it with, so only *your* fleet is colored on your screen.
* **2 Fleets** — players are randomly assigned to one of two massive fleets,
  red and blue, each holding one half of the map (east and west).  Both fleets
  keep their colors for everyone.
* **Party** — a private party realm for you and your friends.

## Defecting

In `2 Fleets` you may defect to the opposing fleet by sailing into its half of
the map and pressing the defect button.  Defecting is blocked while you are
damaged, reloading, near another ship, or being tracked by an enemy weapon —
repair fully, wait for your weapons to reload, shake off enemy weapons, and
move away from other ships first.

# Biomes

The map runs from the tropics in the far south to the Arctic in the far north.

Experienced players may attempt to explore the **Arctic**, located far north.
It is important to understand that the Arctic has three separate types of
terrain: snow, ice sheet, and cracked ice sheet.  Snow, which appears white and
smooth, will damage any ship upon contact.  The two types of ice sheet will slow
and damage most ships, the difference being that non-icebreakers cannot destroy
non-cracked ice sheet.  Submarines can travel beneath both types of ice sheet.

Some ships are tied to a region: icebreakers keep to the Arctic, while dredgers
are kept out of it.

# Hazards

The sea itself will sink you if you are careless:

* Running aground — crashing into the ground.
* Crashing into the border of the map.
* Colliding with other ships, obstacles, or structures.
* Being rammed.

# Ranks

As you play you earn ranks: Ensign, Lieutenant, Commander, Captain, Colonel,
and Admiral.

# Chat

Press **Enter** to focus the chat, type your message, and press **Enter** again
to send.  Remember to never share personal information in chat!
translations.privacy_md:
# Introduction
We collect information to provide, measure, and improve services for all our users. Generally speaking, the amount of personal information we collect is minimal, and you can opt out of providing most of it.

If you are under 18 years of age, we require that you avoid sharing your real name or other personal information in-game, and we recommend asking a trusted adult to help interpret the following information.

# Information we collect
|Information|Collection method|Suggested opt-out method|Primary purpose|Storage duration|
|-|-|-|-|-|
|Alias|Splash screen|Leave blank|Differentiate between players|Forever, e.g. with leaderboard score|
|Team name|Team panel|Don't make team|Differentiate between teams|Forever, e.g. with leaderboard score|
#ifdef chat
|Chat messages|Chat panel|Don't send any|Allow and moderate player communication|Forever, until manually deleted|
#endif
|IP address|Game server|Use a VPN|Security|Forever, e.g. with chat message|
|User agent, referrer|Game server|Use a browser extension to hide|Aggregate or anonymous metrics|Forever|
|How long you play, FPS|Game server|N/A|Aggregate or anonymous metrics|Forever|
#ifdef accounts
|User name|Profile|Don't sign in|Sign in process|Forever, unless you delete your account|
|Nick name|Profile|Leave blank, or don't sign in|Differentiate between players|Forever, unless you delete it|
#ifdef avatar
|Avatar image|Profile|Leave blank, or don't sign in|Differentiate between users|Forever, until manually deleted in Profile|
#endif
|Other information you provide|Profile and Store|Leave blank|Various|Forever, until manually deleted in Profile or Store|
#endif

We do not collect geolocation data or automatically process any data to "profile" you.

# Information we store on your computer
Some game settings, such as language and volume level, are stored in your browser's local storage. To ensure the continuity and consistency of your experience, and provide for internal operations, we store a persistent session identifier in your browser's local storage. We do not use this identifier for advertising purposes.

#ifdef cookie_consent
You can revoke consent for particular non-essential cookies in [settings](/settings/), in which case they will be stored in volatile session storage (not stored on your device).
#endif

You can reset or clear any or all cookies or local storage, at any time, by using your browser's "clear site data" option.

# Information we share with 3rd parties
#ifdef chat
We share your chat messages, including team/whisper chat, with volunteer moderators to help limit inappropriate messages.
#endif

We also use third party services that use cookies, local storage, and/or web beacons for the purpose of online, multi-site behavioral advertising and analytics. These services may collect, share, and/or sell your personal information according to their own privacy policies. We make best efforts to forward, to you, all attempts by such services to obtain your consent or privacy preferences.

# Changes
We reserve the right to alter these privacy policies at any time, without notice.

#ifdef contact_info
# Contact Us
If you have any concern, such as a desire to remove your nickname or your child's nickname from the leaderboard, please contact us by email at [email] or by postal mail at Softbear, Inc. 14150 NE 20th Street #F1-315 Bellevue WA 98007 USA.
#endif
